turns.query: Using dates observed in both the daily Treasury curve and the New York Fed SOFR series, select the date with the lowest reported 10-year-minus-2-year Treasury par-yield spread, breaking an exact tie by the earlier date. Report the eligible common-date count, selected date, its 2-year and 10-year yields, and SOFR. Carry the date forward and interpret the relationship between the two selected measures and its material limits.

Take the 252 Treasury curve observations ending on that selected date. At each date, linearly interpolate the reported 6-month, 1-, 2-, 3-, 5-, 7-, 10-, 20- and 30-year par yields onto the regular half-year grid through 30 years, sequentially bootstrap par instruments, and convert the resulting discount factors to continuously compounded zero yields. Estimate a Diebold-Li dynamic Nelson-Siegel panel with one shared positive decay parameter in [0.01, 5.00] per year and date-specific level, slope and curvature factors by global least squares, choosing the lower decay if an exact objective tie occurs. Report the window boundaries and count, fitted decay, panel zero-yield RMSE, the loading matrix's spectral (2-norm) condition number, and maximum bootstrap par-repricing residual. Carry the decay, loadings and factor history forward, and interpret the curve-fit and numerical diagnostics and the analytical status of the constructed curve.

Using the carried decay and selected-date factor vector, report the level, slope and curvature factors and the fitted continuous zero yields at 2, 10 and 30 years. From the same Nelson-Siegel curve, evaluate the instantaneous forward curve on the 0.25-year grid from 0.25 through 30 years and report its minimum maturity and rate, breaking an exact rate tie by the shorter maturity. Also report the maximum absolute unscaled OLS normal-equation moment max|X' residual| for the selected-date cross-section. Interpret the factor shape and the numerical diagnostic.

Estimate a full intercept-bearing VAR(1) on the carried 252-date DNS factor history and make a one-step factor forecast for the next available Treasury curve date. Report that date, the three forecast factors and the transition matrix's spectral radius. Reconstruct the forecast curve using the carried decay and compare its half-year-grid RMSE against the observed bootstrapped zero curve with the RMSE from a factor random-walk forecast; report both RMSEs and whether the VAR is lower. Interpret this single forecast comparison and its material coverage limits.
